correctness.rationale: The exact 126-vertex graph distances and distance-regular recurrence give five complete adjacency eigenspaces with multiplicities 1,8,27,48,42. Substituting the distance polynomials yields exact powered-distance eigenbranches. Rigorous derivative, AM--GM, and convexity inequalities prove globally that the lambda=1 branch crosses once at p*=0.409576... and the lambda=-4 branch crosses once at p=1, while the other branches stay negative. The centered Gram rank gives dimension 125 below p* and 83 at p*. The standalone checker independently verifies graph distances, recurrences, trace moments, and integer-power spectra; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: KG(9,4) is the first diameter-four odd graph, a canonical 126-point distance-transitive metric. The complete all-exponent powered-distance inertia reveals a nontrivial negative-type threshold with 42 equality directions and a separate eight-mode inertia jump at exponent 1. This exact phase diagram and Hilbert-rank collapse form a motivated benchmark for finite metric embeddings and association-scheme kernel theory rather than an arbitrary subfamily or isolated decimal.
